category_title: Students with IDD in Task Learning Classes (SAT) focused on autonomy and adult life skills
minimal_context: The student is preparing to practice using gardening materials in a cooperative learning group with peers from the ordinary class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are going to practice using the gardening materials. You will be doing this in a cooperative learning group with students from the ordinary class.

STUDENT: I’m learning a lot, to use materials. Gardening, carpentry... I like all.

TUTOR: That is good. Please go over to their table and start working together.

STUDENT: In primary education I was happy with my teachers and classmates. In secondary education, it was hard at the beginning, you need to adapt.

TUTOR: Just go join them and see what they are doing.

STUDENT: I did not get along well with some people in the ordinary class.

options.A: Implement a daily point system, with the daily goal set at earning 80% of the possible points.
options.B: Structure classroom routines, such as signing in and out of the gardening activity, to mimic workplace practices.
options.C: Implement cooperative approaches to learning and planned peer support for the gardening activity.
options.D: Provide a communication book composed of a typed conversational opener with a corresponding picture symbol.
